cards.back: To agree to take or receive something. "She decided to accept the job offer." Common collocations: accept responsibility, accept terms, accept invitation.
A detailed examination of something. "The analysis of the data revealed interesting patterns." Common collocations: data analysis, detailed analysis, critical analysis.
To believe something is true without proof. "We assume that students will complete the assignment." Common collocations: assume responsibility, generally assume, safely assume.
To fasten or join one thing to another. "Please attach the document to your email." Common collocations: attach importance, attach file, firmly attach.
Short in time or length. "The meeting was brief but productive." Common collocations: brief period, brief description, brief moment.
Wide in extent or scope. "The course covers a broad range of topics." Common collocations: broad range, broad perspective, broad support.
An organized effort to achieve a goal. "They launched a campaign to raise awareness." Common collocations: advertising campaign, political campaign, launch campaign.
The main city of a country or money used for investment. "Paris is the capital of France." Common collocations: capital city, raise capital, capital investment.
The maximum amount that something can contain or produce. "The stadium has a capacity of 50,000 people." Common collocations: full capacity, production capacity, storage capacity.
A profession or occupation chosen for long-term work. "He built a successful career in medicine." Common collocations: career path, career development, pursue career.
Something that makes something else happen. "Poor diet is a major cause of health problems." Common collocations: root cause, leading cause, cause concern.
A section of a book or a period in life. "Read chapter three for tomorrow's class." Common collocations: next chapter, new chapter, chapter title.
To state that something is true. "Scientists claim that the treatment is effective." Common collocations: make claim, support claim, false claim.
Traditional and of high quality, serving as a standard. "This novel is a classic of English literature." Common collocations: classic example, classic style, instant classic.
A person you work with in a profession. "I discussed the project with my colleagues." Common collocations: work colleague, senior colleague, former colleague.
A remark expressing an opinion or reaction. "The teacher made several comments on my essay." Common collocations: make comment, add comment, general comment.
To pledge or promise to do something. "The government committed to reducing emissions." Common collocations: commit crime, commit resources, fully commit.
Occurring frequently or shared by many. "It's common for students to feel nervous before exams." Common collocations: common practice, common ground, most common.
To examine similarities and differences. "Compare the results from both experiments." Common collocations: compare prices, compare notes, compare favourably.
Having all necessary parts or to finish something. "Please complete the form by Friday." Common collocations: complete task, complete set, fully complete.
A matter of interest or worry. "Environmental protection is a major concern." Common collocations: major concern, express concern, raise concern.
The state of something or a circumstance affecting something. "The house was in poor condition." Common collocations: medical condition, working condition, necessary condition.
A result or effect of an action. "Climate change has serious consequences for wildlife." Common collocations: negative consequence, direct consequence, unintended consequence.
Large in amount or degree. "The project requires considerable investment." Common collocations: considerable amount, considerable effort, considerable attention.
Communication or connection with someone. "Please contact me if you have questions." Common collocations: make contact, direct contact, lose contact.
To have something inside or include. "This product contains artificial ingredients." Common collocations: contain information, contain errors, fully contain.
To keep happening or doing something. "The meeting will continue after lunch." Common collocations: continue working, continue efforts, continue education.
To persuade someone to believe or do something. "She convinced me to join the team." Common collocations: convince someone, fully convince, hard to convince.
Free from error or to fix mistakes. "Your answer is correct." Common collocations: correct answer, correct mistake, politically correct.
Extremely important or expressing disapproval. "Time management is critical for success." Common collocations: critical thinking, critical point, highly critical.
Relating to the customs and beliefs of a society. "The city offers many cultural activities." Common collocations: cultural diversity, cultural differences, cultural heritage.
Physical harm that reduces value or usefulness. "The storm caused significant damage to buildings." Common collocations: cause damage, serious damage, property damage.
Facts and statistics collected for analysis. "The researchers collected data from 500 participants." Common collocations: collect data, raw data, data analysis.
To bring or transport something to a destination. "The company delivers packages within 24 hours." Common collocations: deliver speech, deliver results, deliver service.
To state that something is not true. "The politician denied the allegations." Common collocations: strongly deny, deny access, deny responsibility.
To find out or decide something. "Tests will determine the cause of the problem." Common collocations: determine outcome, help determine, determine whether.
A tool or piece of equipment for a specific purpose. "Mobile devices have changed how we communicate." Common collocations: electronic device, safety device, storage device.
To give time or effort to something. "She devoted her life to teaching." Common collocations: devote time, devote energy, devote attention.
To be unlike or have different opinions. "Opinions differ on the best approach." Common collocations: differ from, differ significantly, views differ.
A measurable extent or an aspect of a situation. "The building's dimensions are 50 by 30 meters." Common collocations: new dimension, additional dimension, physical dimension.
Straight or to guide toward a target. "Take the most direct route to the airport." Common collocations: direct approach, direct consequence, direct attention.
To show or exhibit something. "The museum displays ancient artifacts." Common collocations: display information, public display, proudly display.
Relating to the home or one's own country. "Domestic flights are cheaper than international ones." Common collocations: domestic affairs, domestic market, domestic violence.
A preliminary version of a document. "Please review the first draft of the report." Common collocations: rough draft, final draft, draft proposal.
Relating to the economy or finance. "The country faces economic challenges." Common collocations: economic growth, economic crisis, economic development.
Achieving maximum productivity with minimum effort. "We need more efficient methods of production." Common collocations: highly efficient, energy efficient, cost efficient.
To completely remove or get rid of something. "The goal is to eliminate poverty worldwide." Common collocations: eliminate risk, eliminate waste, completely eliminate.
A strong feeling such as love, fear, or anger. "Music can stir deep emotions in listeners." Common collocations: strong emotion, show emotion, mixed emotions.
Special importance given to something. "The school places emphasis on academic excellence." Common collocations: place emphasis, special emphasis, great emphasis.
To give work to someone or to use something. "The factory employs over 500 workers." Common collocations: employ staff, employ strategy, self-employed.
